summary: The ad hoc path is close to implementable as written, but the recipe-based path is underspecified; its biggest gap is where the recipe constraints are enforced and what a violation returns, followed by kind's place in captured-input equality and the recipe scaffold.

questions.text: Is the manifest's kind part of captured-input equality, and do MarkReady/MarkDraft preserve it?
questions.reason: Decides whether a kind switch makes acceptance refuse the stale candidate; the ADR says kind is 'captured with its evaluation inputs' and changing it 'invalidates the saved candidate', yet the equality rule lists only revision, name, explanation and before/target/change bytes.

questions.text: Which component enforces the recipe-based constraints (recipe exists, schema/definitions/source/config preserved, state present), against what baseline, and what does a violation return?
questions.reason: Sets the failure semantics and which handler owns the check; the ADR only says to 'compare captured source/configuration as well' and 'Missing state is an error', with no phase, baseline or rejection variant.

questions.text: What does removing an unaccepted workspace delete (candidate dirs, latest pointer), and how is a stale candidate kept from loading under a reused ID?
questions.reason: Allocating max+1 over live directories frees the highest number for reuse, so an old latest/<id> could load against a new workspace; the ADR only says 'Remove only unaccepted workspaces through an explicit operation' and gives no constructor.

questions.text: Is the .kyyn/ candidate store per repository or per KB, and how are latest/<evolution-id> pointers namespaced across KBs?
questions.reason: IDs are unique only per KB, so a repository-root store collides; the ADR says the 'repository and KB prefix come from the explicit load location' but never says where .kyyn/ is rooted.

questions.text: Who computes the Before source validation report shown in preview, and is it stored with the candidate?
questions.reason: Changes EvaluatedEvolution/candidate.dhall shapes and handler rows; the ADR requires that 'Preview surfaces the source validation report separately' but no type or operation carries it.

questions.text: How does CreateEvolution receive the EvolutionKind and RecipeId, and what does the recipe-based scaffold write to change/Evolution.hs?
questions.reason: Shapes the CLI/MCP creation surface and the first draft; the ADR says creation 'selects an ad hoc or recipe-based scaffold from EvolutionKind', but the signature has no kind and only the ad hoc identityEvolution scaffold is shown.

questions.text: Is rebase a Kyyn operation that rewrites the revision and refreshes before/ (and marks Draft), or a manual author edit?
questions.reason: Decides whether an EvolutionAuthoring constructor exists and whether target/ is touched; the ADR says 'rebasing refreshes them' and describes the agent updating Before.revision, but lists no operation.

questions.text: Does RecipeChange's StoredRecipe carry recipe state and its before/after contracts, as RecordedFact carries a RootContract?
questions.reason: Fixes the archived record shape and whether history can be read without recompiling; the ADR says recipe archive records 'retain ... state changes, with before/after contracts and values' but RecipeChange has no contract field.

questions.text: How are RecipeChange entries derived and ordered relative to FactChanges, and do the no-change, whole-contract and duplicate-ID rules apply to them?
questions.reason: Determines report bytes and associativity tests; the ADR gives ordering ('collection identity and FactId') and duplicate rules for facts only.

questions.text: Which PreviewRejection does a host boundary failure that is not a chain mismatch produce, such as duplicate intermediate IDs or a malformed observation value?
questions.reason: Changes how outcomes surface and what tests expect; the ADR maps only chain mismatches to ProposedCodeRejected while saying duplicates are 'rejected at every boundary'.

questions.text: Is the generated evolution ID slug length-limited, and is an over-long name truncated or refused?
questions.reason: An unbounded slug turns into an operational filesystem failure instead of a refusal; the ADR defines the slug alphabet and refuses an empty slug but sets no length.

questions.text: What is the per-save <id> in .kyyn/candidates/<id>/, and how is it generated uniquely?
questions.reason: A fresh directory per save cannot be keyed by evolution ID alone; the ADR says 'writes a fresh .kyyn/candidates/<id>/' and never defines <id>, though any unique private name would do.
